key_insight: A graph neural network trained on smaller GW calculations predicts quasiparticle energy levels in large supercells at a fraction of the computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make accurate electronic-structure modeling more practical for defects, surfaces, and moiré systems where direct GW calculations become prohibitively expensive.
method: Represent atoms as graph nodes and encode interatomic distances on edges.
Use DFT wavefunction projections onto localized atomic orbitals as model features.
Build a targeted, compact GW training dataset and tune hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: For monolayer MoS₂ with a sulfur vacancy, the abstract reports mean absolute errors of 10–50 meV.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the demonstrated defect system remains to be established, and training data must capture the physics of the target simulation.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
